Device Query Conformance Tests

The opt-in query suite checks the Device Interface property contracts in include/qdmi/device.h and include/qdmi/constants.h. It compiles against a provider's prefixed symbols and runs through GoogleTest. It creates no jobs and makes no provider network calls. Supply a controlled local fixture; a fixture that connects to hardware is outside this suite's offline guarantees.

Integration

Use CMake 3.24 or newer and a C++20 compiler. Supply GoogleTest with an existing GTest::gtest_main target and enable CTest in the consuming project. QDMI neither fetches GoogleTest nor enables tests when this helper is merely included. add_subdirectory exposes the helper from a source checkout; find_package(qdmi CONFIG REQUIRED) exposes the same helper and test source from an installation. QDMI's own tests, examples, and templates may all be disabled.

find_package(qdmi CONFIG REQUIRED)
find_package(GTest CONFIG REQUIRED)
enable_testing()
# my-device already supplies MY-prefixed headers and device symbols.
add_qdmi_device_query_tests(
my-query-tests
PREFIX MY
TARGET my-device
FIXTURE_HEADER "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/query_fixture.hpp")

PREFIX is the exact device symbol prefix. TARGET supplies the device library and its public include directories. FIXTURE_HEADER is an existing header; relative paths are resolved against the caller's source directory. Paths may contain spaces. Invoke the helper with distinct executable names to test several devices. On Windows, the helper copies a shared device target's DLL beside the test executable. Other runtime dependencies remain the consumer's responsibility. Tests have distinct executable-name prefixes and the CTest label qdmi-query.

The header defines QDMIQueryFixture, derived from ::testing::Test, with a protected initialized session named session of the prefixed session type. Initialize the device once in SetUpTestSuite, allocate and initialize a session in SetUp, free it in TearDown, and finalize the device in TearDownTestSuite. Check setup errors with GoogleTest assertions and make cleanup safe after partial setup. GoogleTest supplies main; do not define another one. See test/query/example_fixture.hpp for a complete offline example, and test/query/consumer for a separate project that opts in twice.

cmake --build build --target my-query-tests
ctest --test-dir build -L qdmi-query --output-on-failure

Dependency configuration may download packages. Test execution needs no credentials or provider access. The example's token is only a local placeholder. Ordinary consumers that do not call the helper acquire no query executable or GoogleTest dependency.

Checked Contracts

For each supported property the suite checks support-only and size-only queries, exact and oversized typed buffers, optional size_ret, and one-byte-short buffers. It validates scalar types, string termination, array element sizes, defined enum values, and advertised nonnull handles. Invalid enums, removed device property IDs 8 and 9, and isolated null arguments are checked against the specified errors. Error returns may overwrite the supplied buffer.

Device coverage includes name, version, library version, ID, status, qubit count, queue length, site and operation lists, coupling map, child devices, supported program formats, length and duration units and scale factors, and minimum atom distance. Site coverage includes name, mandatory index, T1, T2, coordinates, zone status, spatial extents, module index, and submodule index. Operation coverage includes name, qubit and parameter counts, duration, fidelity, interaction and blocking radii, idling fidelity, zone status, site tuples, and mean shuttling speed. Relationships include distinct site indices and supported coordinate triples, coupling endpoints in advertised sites, and conditional unit availability. The installed headers remain the normative reference.

The table uses suffixes from the source enums QDMI_Device_Property, QDMI_Site_Property, and QDMI_Operation_Property in constants.h. The query error and buffer contracts are defined in device.h. All payloads receive the buffer checks above; the final column records additional support rules.

Property suffix (source enum prefix omitted) Payload Required support / assertions
DEVICE: NAME, VERSION, LIBRARYVERSION, ID char string Optional directly; no name, version format, or client ID stability assumptions
DEVICE: STATUS QDMI_Device_Status Optional; scalar shape and one defined status, excluding MAX
DEVICE: QUBITSNUM, QUEUELENGTH size_t Optional; no equality with site count or queue stability
DEVICE: SITES prefixed QDMI_Site array Optional; query only advertised nonnull handles
DEVICE: OPERATIONS prefixed QDMI_Operation array Optional; query only advertised nonnull handles
DEVICE: COUPLINGMAP prefixed QDMI_Site array Optional; even length; endpoints belong to SITES when available
DEVICE: LENGTHUNIT, DURATIONUNIT char string Required when related length/duration values are supported; nonempty string; unit notation remains unspecified
DEVICE: LENGTHSCALEFACTOR, DURATIONSCALEFACTOR double Optional; unsupported means default 1.0; no invented numeric bounds
DEVICE: MINATOMDISTANCE uint64_t Optional; requires LENGTHUNIT
DEVICE: SUPPORTEDPROGRAMFORMATS QDMI_Program_Format array Optional; empty allowed; defined regular/custom formats only; no job calls
DEVICE: CHILDDEVICES prefixed QDMI_Child_Device array Optional; no child configuration or job calls
DEVICE: numeric 8, 9 none Must return NOTSUPPORTED with a valid session
SITE: INDEX size_t Mandatory per advertised site; unique, sparse and unsorted allowed
SITE: T1, T2 uint64_t Optional per site; requires DURATIONUNIT
SITE: NAME char string Optional per site
SITE: XCOORDINATE, YCOORDINATE, ZCOORDINATE int64_t Optional per site; requires LENGTHUNIT; complete coordinate triples unique
SITE: ISZONE bool Optional; unsupported means false
SITE: XEXTENT, YEXTENT, ZEXTENT uint64_t Optional on zones; NOTSUPPORTED on nonzones; requires LENGTHUNIT
SITE: MODULEINDEX, SUBMODULEINDEX uint64_t Optional; grouping IDs need not be unique per site
OPERATION: NAME char string Optional context-free
OPERATION: QUBITSNUM, PARAMETERSNUM size_t Optional context-free
OPERATION: DURATION uint64_t Optional context-free; requires DURATIONUNIT
OPERATION: FIDELITY, IDLINGFIDELITY double Optional context-free; no inferred [0,1] bound
OPERATION: INTERACTIONRADIUS, BLOCKINGRADIUS uint64_t Optional context-free; requires LENGTHUNIT
OPERATION: ISZONED bool Optional context-free; unsupported means false
OPERATION: SITES prefixed QDMI_Site array Optional context-free; membership; local tuple width when arity available; zone membership for global operations when site classification available
OPERATION: MEANSHUTTLINGSPEED uint64_t Optional context-free; requires both units
DEVICE/SITE/OPERATION: MAX none Invalid enum; require INVALIDARGUMENT with other arguments valid
DEVICE/SITE/OPERATION: CUSTOM1..CUSTOM5 implementation-defined Deliberately unqueried: neither type nor support is generic

Optional unsupported properties skip when no advertised object supports them. Mixed support across objects is valid; mandatory site index support is checked on every advertised site. Empty arrays and sparse indices are valid. Site counts need not equal qubit counts, since sites may represent zones. Direct device ID support is optional; the client-visible stable-ID rule is separate. Repeated metadata values need not stay equal. Metadata growth during retrieval is reported explicitly; use controlled metadata for reproducible results. Payloads above the suite's 64 MiB allocation limit fail with a diagnostic; that is a harness limit, not a QDMI size restriction.

Exclusions and Specification Follow-up

The suite does not create jobs, compile programs, set session parameters, load providers, or validate credentials. It does not probe fabricated, foreign, freed, or uninitialized handles. Custom properties have implementation-defined types and are excluded. Operation queries use zero site and parameter counts with null inputs; context-dependent metadata is excluded. It adds no undocumented numerical bounds, gate names, ordering, or topology symmetry requirements.

The suite assumes valid native scalar object representations. ABI-invalid or memory-corrupting providers require separate memory-safety and sanitizer checks.

Unit strings are checked for nonempty content, shape, and conditional availability. The headers do not define accepted symbols, spellings, or aliases, so unit notation needs a separate specification decision. Radius and idling-fidelity applicability and zero-arity local-operation tuple semantics also need clarification before adding stronger assertions. The suite does not change the normative API docstrings.

QDMI CI runs positive controls and fixed negative controls for malformed sizes, invalid properties, empty units, missing mandatory indices, omitted size outputs, and missing string terminators at every retrieval position. It also runs two source consumers and relocated installed consumers on Linux and macOS. The consumer checks include fixture/install paths with spaces, missing installed assets, and explicit opt-out. This workflow does not run on Windows; local Windows verification is separate.
